concerns.concern: None of the four parts of the proposed mechanism is measured: gate-induced alignment of polar nanoregions, remnant polarization at zero gate, randomization by light, and oxygen-vacancy charge-state switching. There are no polarization, structural or charge-state probes, so the mechanism is a hypothesis rather than a result.
concerns.quote: No direct evidence for PNR alignment, remnant polarization or OV charge-state switching.

concerns.concern: The T_c changes may simply follow disorder and mobility: higher T_c always comes with higher sheet resistance and lower mobility, which matches prior KTO(111) gating work. The authors have not checked whether all states fall on one T_c-versus-mobility or T_c-versus-resistance curve, which would make the polar-nanoregion picture unnecessary.
concerns.quote: A simpler disorder/mobility explanation of the T_c changes is not tested.

concerns.concern: The dielectric spectra were taken in only one unspecified sample state. The paper never shows that permittivity, loss or the strengths of the two relaxation peaks differ between gate-cycled and illuminated states, which is the minimal test that these excitations carry the memory.
concerns.quote: The dielectric spectra were also measured in a single, unspecified state of the sample.

concerns.concern: The capacitance is measured across the whole 0.5 mm substrate, so it is a bulk-averaged response rather than an interface-specific one. A conducting surface layer on an insulating bulk can produce thermally activated loss peaks through Maxwell–Wagner relaxation, and this and other artefacts (Schottky contact, depletion layer, AlOx, defect hopping) are not excluded.
concerns.quote: A conducting, OV-rich surface layer on an insulating bulk is a textbook Maxwell–Wagner (interfacial-polarization) configuration.

concerns.concern: The well-known back-gate trap-escape mechanism from LAO/STO could explain the first-cycle irreversibility, the threshold near −17 V and the persistent resistance and mobility changes without polar nanoregions. It is not discussed, the relevant literature is not cited, and the claimed tunnelling into deep donors is asserted rather than tested.
concerns.quote: The established back-gate trap-escape mechanism is neither discussed nor excluded.

concerns.concern: The Hall density is higher at −50 V than at +50 V, which is the opposite of what the field effect would give. This sign reversal is not discussed.
concerns.quote: This is opposite to the naive field-effect expectation and is not discussed.

concerns.concern: The measured density change over the gate sweep is several times larger than the simple capacitive estimate for a 0.5 mm dielectric with the measured permittivity.
concerns.quote: Δn ≈ 4–5×10¹² cm⁻² over the sweep, several times the capacitive estimate ε₀εV/d.

concerns.concern: The text contradicts itself on carrier flow: one place says gate cycles increase n and another says they decrease it. The same negative gate branch is also used to explain electrons moving both into and out of the 2DEG.
concerns.quote: The same branch is invoked for opposite charge flows.

concerns.concern: There is no charge accounting. The integrated gate-current transient appears to far exceed the Hall density change, and leakage is not separated from displacement current, so it is unknown where the displaced charge ends up.
concerns.quote: Leakage through the substrate and contacts is not separated from displacement current.

concerns.concern: The T_c shifts are only tens of mK, a fraction of the 0.2–0.3 K transition width. T_c is defined at 50% of a normal-state resistance that itself changes by 5–8%, so the shifts may reflect normalization or inhomogeneity rather than pairing; no other criteria, widths or error bars are given.
concerns.quote: The T_c shifts are small relative to the transition width and rest on a single, normalization-sensitive criterion.

concerns.concern: Illumination is never shown to return T_c or resistance to the pristine pre-gating value. Pristine and illuminated values are quoted at different temperatures, and the authors themselves say the system does not fully recover.
concerns.quote: "Complete erasure" is not demonstrated.

concerns.concern: The authors do not give a microscopic pathway for how 1.97 eV photons would randomize polar-nanoregion orientations. Local heating or photo-screening are not considered.
concerns.quote: Photon energy is not a natural variable for dipole reorientation, so local heating or photo-screening must be considered.

concerns.concern: No quantitative model reproduces the sign and magnitude of the changes in resistance, density and mobility, for example trap-occupancy rate equations coupled to a confinement calculation with field-dependent permittivity.
concerns.quote: develop at least a minimal quantitative model that reproduces the sign and magnitude of ΔR_s, Δn and Δμ

concerns.concern: The extracted permittivity is well below bulk KTO values and is not explained. Possible causes include dead layers or depletion regions that would distort the loss, geometric errors, the large ac amplitude, or the reduced region.
concerns.quote: The extracted ε (~1500–2000 at low T, ~1600 quoted) is well below bulk KTO values (~4000–4500).

concerns.concern: The dielectric analysis ignores the finite sheet resistance of the 2DEG and the wiring. No equivalent-circuit or full impedance analysis is given.
concerns.quote: The analysis also neglects the finite 2DEG sheet resistance (~800 Ω) and the wiring.

concerns.concern: Permittivity was measured only at zero dc bias, although KTO permittivity depends strongly on field within the ±50 V range actually used.
concerns.quote: ε was measured only at zero dc bias, although ε(E) in KTO is strongly field-dependent within the ±50 V range used.

concerns.concern: The loss peaks are assigned to polar nanoregions and oxygen-vacancy ionization only by analogy with the literature. Alternatives such as off-centre impurities, polaronic hopping, defect-dipole complexes or Maxwell–Wagner relaxation are not excluded, and substrate impurity content is not characterized.
concerns.quote: Assignment of the loss peaks rests on literature analogy

concerns.concern: The peak fits are poorly documented. Peaks are marked on weak, noisy curves, the Arrhenius fits cover a narrow temperature range, no uncertainties or attempt frequencies are given, and the fitting procedure is not described.
concerns.quote: No uncertainties are given for T_p, E_a or the attempt frequencies ω₁, ω₂, and the peak-fitting procedure is not described.

concerns.concern: The correlation between the gate-induced change and permittivity is non-discriminating, because both vary monotonically with temperature. The two regimes rest on a few points with no fit statistics, and the steeper low-temperature slope has other explanations.
concerns.quote: Both are monotonic functions of temperature, so the parametric plot (Fig. 3d) will be smooth and near-linear for almost any mechanism.

concerns.concern: The proposed proportionality between the gate-induced change and (ε − ε_∞) is not derived. It describes gate efficiency rather than oxygen-vacancy charge exchange specifically.
concerns.quote: The proposed Δ_L ∝ (ε − ε_∞), on the grounds that "larger ε gives a stronger displacement field", is not derived.

concerns.concern: The timescales do not match. Extrapolating the dielectric Arrhenius laws to the very low effective frequencies of gate sweeps and dark relaxation gives about 25 K and 80 K, not the claimed 35 K and 95 K.
concerns.quote: Extrapolating the Arrhenius laws with plausible prefactors to these frequencies gives roughly 25 K and 80 K, not 35 K and 95 K.

concerns.concern: The description of the relaxation time versus temperature contradicts the plot: 95 K is a local maximum, not a minimum. Adjacent points jump by about 50%, suggesting scatter or unstable fits.
concerns.quote: The plotted data show minima near ~30–35 K and ~85–90 K, while 95 K is a sharp local maximum

concerns.concern: The dark-relaxation maxima at 35 K and 95 K each rest on essentially one point, with coarse temperature sampling and no repeat runs. The 95 K trace is noisy and non-monotonic, suggesting temperature instability or heating.
concerns.quote: Each maximum (Fig. 4b, 35 K and 95 K) rests on essentially one point, with coarse temperature sampling and no repeat runs.

concerns.concern: A single-exponential fit is used for relaxation that is likely stretched or multi-component. This makes the extracted time constants and amplitudes depend on the fit model, and the non-monotonic behaviour could come from overlapping relaxations.
concerns.quote: A single-exponential fit to likely stretched or multi-component (glassy PPC) relaxation makes τ and ΔR fit-model dependent.

concerns.concern: The claimed energetic preference for partially aligned polar nanoregions and ionized vacancies in an interfacial potential trap is invoked without any model.
concerns.quote: is invoked without a model.

concerns.concern: The LED is driven at fixed voltage but its output depends on temperature, so the photon flux and starting state vary with temperature. The flux at the sample is unknown.
concerns.quote: Photon flux, and hence the starting state, therefore varies with temperature, and the flux at the sample is unknown.

concerns.concern: Heating by the LED is not quantified, so the optical erasure could partly be thermal annealing. A dark heating control is needed.
concerns.quote: "optical" erasure could partly be thermal annealing

concerns.concern: Only one wavelength (630 nm) is used, so there is no spectral threshold to identify the defect levels involved.
concerns.quote: Only one wavelength (630 nm) is used, so no spectral threshold is available to identify the defect levels involved.

concerns.concern: Density and mobility come from a single-band Hall analysis of a likely multi-band 2DEG. This can confuse band-occupation changes with total-density changes at the 1–5% level the mechanism relies on.
concerns.quote: This can conflate changes in band occupation and mobility ratio with changes in total density.

concerns.concern: The data combine three separate protocol runs in a strongly history-dependent system, but reproducibility of the starting state is not shown and no error bars are given.
concerns.quote: run-to-run reproducibility of the starting state must be shown, but no error bars are given.

concerns.concern: The conversion from van der Pauw measurements to sheet resistance via finite-element modelling, and any transport anisotropy of KTO(111), are not documented.
concerns.quote: The van der Pauw-to-R_s conversion via FEM, and the possible anisotropy of KTO(111) transport (Ref. 16), are not documented.

concerns.concern: All data appear to come from one device. There are no controls with different AlOx thickness, reduction, orientation or a non-superconducting sample to separate interface effects from substrate-bulk effects.
concerns.quote: All data appear to come from a single device, without controls.

concerns.concern: The memristive, neuromorphic and quantum-memristor framing is not backed by device data. Writing and erasing require harsh conditions, and no retention, endurance, variance, level count, speed or energy metrics are given.
concerns.quote: The memristive, neuromorphic and quantum-memristor framing is not supported by device-level data.

concerns.concern: Novelty is overstated. Prior work already reports gate-cycling-enhanced superconductivity at STO and KTO interfaces, and related hysteresis, trapping, photoconductivity and glassy-dynamics studies are not discussed or differentiated.
concerns.quote: The claim of a "previously unrecognized interplay" should be recalibrated accordingly.

concerns.concern: The dependence of the final resistance on cycle order (Type A vs B) may simply reflect which branch of the known hysteresis loop the sweep ends on, not an internal state variable.
concerns.quote: The Type A/B sequence dependence may be trivially branch-dependent.

concerns.concern: Protocol and measurement details are missing: sweep rates, hold times, leakage levels, LED power at the sample, dielectric measurement geometry and fringe corrections, and which frequency is plotted in Fig. 3a.
concerns.quote: sweep rates, hold times and gate-leakage levels in the main-text protocols

concerns.concern: There are textual, labelling and caption errors: a duplicated sentence, a mislabelled resistance value, caption–text inconsistencies, a mislabelled supplementary figure, misused terms and typos.
concerns.quote: Textual, labelling and caption errors.
